uncited: This family of methods extends static NeRF architectures to model dynamic human subjects, enabling novel view synthesis and pose extrapolation for animatable avatars.
It addresses the limitations of standard NeRF, which overfits to static scenes and lacks the structural priors necessary to generalize across different poses or unseen subjects.

The core task of a NeRF network architecture is to learn a continuous volumetric scene representation $F_\Theta: (\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}) \rightarrow (\sigma, \mathbf{c})$, where $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the spatial position, $\mathbf{d} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the viewing direction, $\sigma$ is the volume density, and $\mathbf{c} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ is the view-dependent color.
The rendering process integrates these outputs along rays using standard volume rendering equations.

Numbers indicate feature dimensions. '+' indicates concatenation.
The modeling of dynamic human subjects in neural radiance fields emerged as a distinct sub-area following the success of static NeRF.
Impactful works in this domain include Neural Head Avatar (December 2021) [219], IMAvatar (December 2021) [220], and INSTA (November 2022) [221].

By integrating parametric body models (like SMPL) or deformable mesh representations with neural radiance fields, these methods decouple geometry and appearance, allowing for high-fidelity rendering of complex human dynamics and clothing details that implicit fields alone struggle to capture [S1, S2].

The evidence explicitly states that the method leverages 'SMPL geometry priors' (parametric body models) and uses a 'human NeRF model' (neural radiance fields). It further notes that the approach learns 'extra geometry details beyond the SMPL model' and uses Mask-RCNN to estimate 2D details such as 'hair and clothes' (clothing details). Additionally, the comparison with NeuralBody highlights that the proposed method generalizes better and renders faithfully, implying it overcomes limitations (like overfitting) that other implicit field methods might struggle with. Thus, the claim that integrating these models decouples geometry and appearance to capture complex dynamics and clothing details is supported by the text.
